page.title: Guides · tinyactors
page.description: Steps for each task with tinyactors, from writing a chart to running millions of actors, each with a program that runs.

hero.headline: Steps for each task, with programs that run
hero.lede: Each program shown with its output runs in the site's tests against the published package, and must print what the page shows.

item.text: A chart's code is JavaScript that reads the actor's variables by name, and your charts compile into one image.
A payment that retries every 30 seconds runs all its attempts in a test that takes milliseconds.
A chart your users upload runs in a separate engine, where a runaway loop ends in an error.

section.heading: Connect actors to your code and other hosts

item.text: A chart asks for outside work by sending an event, and an object of yours answers with another.
A connection opens when a chart enters a state and closes when it leaves.
An actor sends to an actor on another machine by its address, over a wire you write.

term.link: When the actor is not there

item.text: Choose, for each kind of actor, what a send does when its target is not running.
A started actor takes about 530 bytes on Node.js, and a hibernated one about 120.
Two million actors ran with at most 1000 in memory and the rest as bytes in a database.
Running actors move to their chart's next version and keep the state they reached.
A host of two million actors copies into a 165 MB snapshot that another process restores.
Record every input your program gives a host, and one loop rebuilds every actor after a crash.
Ask a running actor which state it is in, and count what each chart has done.
Each step an actor takes becomes a span in your OpenTelemetry collector.
Change one import, and your charts run in a page or a Worker.
